Financial-crime controls remain under scrutiny, while regulators are asking how banks can deploy generative and agentic AI without weakening accountability, client protection or resilience.

📌 In March, MAS and 24 industry participants released the MindForge AI Risk Management Toolkit, covering traditional, generative and agentic AI.

📌 In May, MAS began working with five banks, GovTech and the Singapore Police Force on a secure AI/ML proof-of-value using pooled data to improve scam detection.

This is directly relevant to AI use in KYC, source-of-wealth reviews, advisory preparation and client servicing.

𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗞𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗱𝗼𝗺: 𝗔𝗜 𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗺𝗲𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗶𝗰-𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗸 𝘀𝗰𝗿𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘆
📌 The FCA’s July Mills Review examines how advanced AI and autonomous agents could reshape financial advice, product selection and portfolio management by 2030.

📌 The Bank of England warned in July that frontier AI has increased cyber and operational-resilience risks. From 13 July, Microsoft, Google Cloud, AWS and Oracle also fall within the UK’s Critical Third Parties regime.

𝗦𝘄𝗶𝘁𝘇𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱: 𝘁𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗔𝗠𝗟 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗔𝗜 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆
📌 FINMA also issued guidance on digital fraud and proposed tighter AML requirements around beneficial ownership, control structures and sanctions compliance.

📌 KPMG’s 2026 study found 79.5% of surveyed Swiss private banks had deployed AI. Yet 76.5% remained at an ad hoc or developing stage, and only four of 73 assessed qualified as AI leaders.
